title: Human-induced climate change

match.reason: No bank point teaches the human causes of extra greenhouse gases; the closest, The greenhouse effect, covers the natural mechanism and is pitched at Year 9, while the others cover evidence and mitigation or adaptation.

draft.title: Human-induced climate change
card: Human activities add extra greenhouse gases to the air. Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide. Farming releases methane, for example from cattle and rice paddies.
Forests take in carbon dioxide as they grow. Clearing and burning them releases the carbon they stored and leaves fewer trees to take in more.
More greenhouse gases in the air mean more of the heat radiated from Earth's surface is trapped. The planet's average temperature rises. This is global warming.

A warmer planet changes the climate, which is the pattern of weather over many years. Effects include melting ice, rising sea levels and more extreme heat. Climate change caused by people is called human-induced climate change.
draft.remember: People add greenhouse gases and remove forests, so more heat is trapped and the climate changes.

a.q: Which action adds extra greenhouse gas to the air and so contributes to human-induced climate change?
opts: Natural weathering of rocks over time
A plant taking in carbon dioxide to grow
a.why: Burning coal releases carbon dioxide that was stored underground, which adds to the greenhouse gases in the air. Planting a forest does the opposite, because growing trees take in carbon dioxide.
a.clue: Which option puts more greenhouse gas into the air because of people?

b.q: A company clears a large area of forest in Gippsland to make farmland for cattle. How does this change add to climate change?
opts: It releases stored carbon and cattle add methane
It adds methane only, as cleared land holds no carbon
It removes heat from the air, but cattle add carbon
It adds carbon dioxide only, as cattle make no gas
b.why: Clearing forest releases the carbon the trees stored and leaves fewer trees to take in carbon dioxide. Cattle also release methane, so both changes add greenhouse gases. The other options each leave out one of these effects or get one wrong.
b.clue: Think about what happens to the trees and what the cattle give off.

b.best: It releases stored carbon and cattle add methane
